seventeenth_tool_spike_feasibility.estimated_effort: 60-120 minutes for a foundation-only tool; longer for model-backed handler, composition-specific projections, evals, and docs.
why_feasible: SKILL_TEMPLATE.md exists and all 16 tool skills follow the same nine-section order.
Registry helper auto-fills v2 defaults, schemas, persistence posture, default ContextProvider projection, side effects, and skill file path.
Audit scripts catch count, schema, ontology, handler-contract, skill presence, and projection-file existence.
why_not_one_folder_yet: Marketplace registry is a central MARKETPLACE_TOOLS array, not one file per tool or import.meta.glob discovery.
A new tool requires adding a handler contract to src/lib/tools/marketplace/handler-contracts.ts.
The audit enforces exactly 16 tools, so a real 17th-tool spike would fail until the cap/gate is intentionally changed.
Canary status is declared case IDs, not an executable canary fixture harness.

findings.title: Marketplace handlers are prompt-contract foundation runs, not specialist model-backed tool handlers.
evidence: src/lib/tools/marketplace/handler-contracts.ts executionStage is prompt-contract for every tool.
src/lib/tools/marketplace/runner.ts emits deterministic-foundation-with-handler-contract posture.
docs/audits/2026-05-06-COMPREHENSIVE.md lists specialist model-backed marketplace handlers as a remaining launch gap.
findings.impact: The marketplace can run and persist artifacts, but it should not be represented as fully specialist analytical execution.

findings.title: Skill conformance script name is an alias to presence checks and does not itself enforce order.

findings.impact: Current files are ordered correctly, but CI would not catch future section reordering unless the script is strengthened.
